name: Fauchon L Hotel Kyoto
positioning: FAUCHON L'Hotel Kyoto, a city hotel by the Paris gourmet house FAUCHON on the Kamo River, with interiors that pair FAUCHON pink, black and gold with Japanese design touches
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable base for Gion and Higashiyama
Food and pastry lovers drawn to the FAUCHON brand
Couples looking for a design-led stay with spa rituals

facts.text: The hotel is located along the Kamo River, often referred to as Kyoto's Seine River.
The hotel is within a 10-minute walk of Gion, Higashiyama and Shijo Kawaramachi.
The hotel is a 6-minute walk from Kiyomizu-Gojo Station on the Keihan Line.
The design blends FAUCHON style in magenta, black and gold with nods to Kyoto, including black painted bamboo accents on the walls.
Sakura petals appear in many design elements, including the lobby ceiling lights and the fabrics in the guest rooms and suites.
Suites are decorated in FAUCHON pink, white, black and gold on Japanese fabrics and textiles.
The Fauchon Suite has a separate living room, bedroom, bathroom and walk-in closet.
Le Spa FAUCHON is the world's first spa named after FAUCHON, in partnership with Credo International and KOS PARIS.
The Grand Cafe FAUCHON is on the top floor, with a panoramic view of Higashiyama.
Teatime features a pink teapot, macarons and a tea blend, One Night In Kyoto, created especially for the hotel.
A specially curated playlist mixes French and Japanese music.
The hotel offers exclusive private tours and curated experiences of Kyoto.

highlights.text: Every room and suite has a FAUCHON Gourmet Bar, a reimagined minibar in a cabinet custom-crafted by Roche Bobois and designer Sacha Lakic, stocked with FAUCHON products including champagne and sweet and savory treats.
The spa offers an optional Private Bath Ritual with a pink bathtub with rose petals floating on top.
Washi paper lines the wall above the headboards in the guest rooms, and the bedside lighting represents the French millefeuille pastry.
Higashiyama-view rooms look out on Kiyomizu-dera and the Higashiyama hills.

considerations.text: There is no parking lot at the hotel; public transportation, a taxi or car service is recommended.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
